_label: POST-HOC ADDITION (T8, labelled). Frozen letter->Basel-III-ECRA-risk-weight map for the capital recast. Own hash in MANIFEST_CAPITAL.sha256; does NOT enter the sealed MANIFEST_INPUTS. No model calls; regulatory retrieval only, quote-verified.

verification.source_document: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), consolidated Basel Framework, CRE20 'Standardised approach: individual exposures'
verification.paragraph: CRE20.42 and its accompanying 'Risk weight table for corporate exposures' (External Credit Risk Assessment Approach, ECRA)
verification.quote_intro: "For corporate exposures of banks incorporated in jurisdictions that allow the use of external ratings for regulatory purposes, banks will assign 'base' risk weights according to [the] table" (CRE20.42).
verification.verbatim_check: The rendered CRE20 table returns exactly: AAA to AA- 20% | A+ to A- 50% | BBB+ to BBB- 75% | BB+ to BB- 100% | Below BB- 150% | Unrated 100%. This matches the expected ECRA shape; no memory-based values were used.

us_implementation_note: BIS ECRA is the load-bearing standard here. US implementation differs: Dodd-Frank Act section 939A prohibits US banking agencies from relying on external credit ratings, so the US standardized approach does NOT use this ratings-based ECRA table. Under the current US standardized approach most corporate exposures carry a flat 100% risk weight (the 2023 US 'Basel III endgame' proposal added a 65% weight for certain 'investment grade' corporates with publicly traded securities). We use the BIS ECRA table as primary because the elicitation produces letter ratings; the US flat-100% variant is noted for context and used only as a robustness sensitivity, not as the primary map.
scale_reference: Maps the 21-grade elicitation scale in rating_scale.json (AAA..C) onto ECRA base risk weights.

capital_function.pillar: Pillar 1 minimum only (no capital conservation buffer, no G-SIB/countercyclical/systemic buffers, no Pillar 2)
capital_function.EAD_assumption: Exposure-at-default = stated notional per name (equal-weight $1B base case); credit conversion factors and CRM not applied (on-balance-sheet drawn corporate exposure assumed).

ambiguity_flags: COARSENING BELOW BB-: the ECRA table has a single 'Below BB-' row at 150%, so every elicitation grade from B+ through C (B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C) collapses to the SAME 150% risk weight. The capital map is therefore COARSER than the 21-grade elicitation scale in the sub-BB- region. Any verdict that lands anywhere in distress produces an identical 150% weight -> capital dispersion mechanically saturates once a name reaches B+ or worse. This interacts directly with the market-pricing saturation finding and MUST be reported alongside the capital dispersion, not hidden.

IG/HY vs capital boundary mismatch: the ECRA 100% row is BB+ to BB- (already high-yield), while the 75% row ends at BBB-. The capital step across the IG/HY boundary (BBB- 75% -> BB+ 100%) is a 25pp risk-weight jump; the largest single-notch capital jump is BB- 100% -> B+ 150% (50pp).
No separate CCC/CC/C capital resolution exists in the standardized approach; distinctions the model draws among CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C are invisible to Pillar 1 capital.
sources: BCBS, Basel Framework CRE20 (Standardised approach: individual exposures), para 20.42 and the corporate ECRA risk weight table, in force 2023-01-01. https://www.bis.org/basel_framework/chapter/CRE/20.htm
Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (2010), section 939A (removal of references to credit ratings) — basis for the US non-ratings standardized approach (context note only).
